reason: An xsi:type of `:a:b` under a default xmlns reads as the datatype a:b in the default namespace. #570, and docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md (PROV-XML section) says 3.3.0 reads the 3.2.3 shape as the default namespace's name.

A bundle's own default namespace, read from XML, is written back on its bundleContent element and reads again as an equal document. #572 (the writer dropped a bundle's own default namespace), and docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md (PROV-XML section) says it round trips.

A bundle named under a prefix declared only on its bundleContent leaves the document with no namespaces, gives the bundle that prefix, and round trips through PROV-N, PROV-JSON and PROV-XML. #572 and docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md (PROV-XML section), which say a bundleContent prefix registers on the bundle.

A name in the default namespace is written as a bare QName under xmlns, and one with a colon takes a prefix bound to the IRI, minted as dn or reused when declared, in every position and in a bundle. #570 and #677, and docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md (PROV-XML section).

A name whose prefix the element does not declare, in each position a name is read, raises ProvXMLException with the line, the element and the model's sentence, whether or not the document declares an xmlns (#677). Proposed to narrow by the rows "3.2.3 bare id, default" and "3.2.3 bare id, no xmlns", and kept. docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md names the input, a 3.2.3 file holding prov:id="a:b" for a default-namespace local part, and planning/specs/2026-10-23-release-3.3.0-spec3-names-provn.md lists a 3.2.3-shaped prov:id="a:b" file rejected among the cases to pin under ruling N69. The judge's probe of the 3.2.3 wheel shows that 3.2.3 also wrote a bare prov:id="a:b" with no xmlns, for a name in a bundle's own default inside bundleContent, while the second row puts the name at the top level. Both rows come from one table entry. The rows "record id, default" and "record id, no xmlns" take the same path through `xml_qname_to_QualifiedName` and `resolve_name`, and the verifier's only separating fault was keyed on the literal a:b, which the judge treated as contrived.

Names that the element's namespaces resolve read to the expected IRIs, for an empty prefix, reference text, a prefix on the root or on the reference, an attribute element, and whitespace around QName text. #677, and docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md (PROV-XML section).

The names "e" and ":e" on an element that declares its own xmlns raise the xmlns-on-an-element sentence, with or without a document default. #677, and docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md (PROV-XML section) lists the error. Took over the job of the removed test_xml.py::test_nested_default_namespace, which read a fixture with an entity element that declares its own xmlns and a bare prov:id under a root that declares only prov. Its row "e-no xmlns" reads the same shape from a string and asserts the full message that `_bare_name` raises, which names the IRI and the name, where the removed test asserted a regex on the IRI and a substring. The verifier's fault in `_bare_name` that dropped the IRI from the message failed all four rows with the removed test deselected, and its fault that rejected only a root declaring just prov failed the rows "e-no xmlns" and ":e-no xmlns".

A prefix declared on bundleContent registers on that bundle with its own IRI, and the document keeps its own binding, whether the bundle comes before or after a record that uses the document's prefix. docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md (PROV-XML section) says a prefix declared on prov:bundleContent is registered on the bundle, and planning/specs/2026-10-23-release-3.3.0-spec3-names-provn.md settles it.

A prefix that an element inside bundleContent rebinds to another IRI reads as a fresh prefix ex_1 on the bundle, while the document keeps ex. planning/specs/2026-10-23-release-3.3.0-spec3-names-provn.md (the use-then-bind paragraph) says the reader gives such a binding ex_1.

An xsd:QName or prov:QUALIFIED_NAME value whose prefix only the XML declares reads as a qualified name in that namespace. docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md (PROV-XML section) says a prefix declared in scope resolves.

Removed. A generation with an activity, no identifier and no time read back from XML equal to the original, with None for prov:time in `ProvRecord.formal_attributes`. It guarded the rule that the fix for empty-string values must leave an absent optional attribute None. #224 reports only empty-string values that vanished, and the absent-attribute guard comes from the message of commit c1715ca0, which cites #224. test_statements.py::test_generation_2 takes over, because its xml row round trips a generation with an activity and no time (identifier ex:gen2) and compares documents, so an empty-string time would be an extra attribute and fail equality. The judge's reader fault, an empty-string prov:time appended in `ProvXMLSerializer._read_record` for a generation read without one, failed test_statements.py::test_generation_2, and test_statements.py::test_generation_1 and test_statements.py::test_generation_3 as well. The judge's model fault, an empty string for a missing value in `ProvRecord.formal_attributes`, escapes equality but failed test_model.py::test_flattening, test_model.py::test_unifying and test_model.py::test_add_bundle_document among dozens of other tests. A reader fault limited to a generation with no identifier passes test_statements.py::test_generation_2 but failed 20 or more shared round-trip and read tests. The removal check found no arc that only the removed tests cover and no mutant of provxml.py or records.py that became undetected.
Reading a document with nested internal entity definitions raises lxml's XMLSyntaxError. docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-XML section) says the reader does not expand a DOCTYPE entity, and #273.

A blank reference element with no prov:ref raises ProvXMLException saying it has no prov:ref. docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-XML section) says a reference with neither prov:ref nor text raises ProvXMLException.

The xsd and xsi prefixes declared on bundleContent register nothing on the bundle. The contract is the rule of PR #649 that a bundle registers only what it binds (commit 490ce0f8). The argument names `_own_prefixes`, which leaves the built-in IRIs out of a bundle's own prefixes, and `ProvXMLSerializer._build_nsmap`, which declares a bundle's own prefixes on bundleContent, from reading, with no planted fault behind them. It guards against a fault a probe showed. A bundle that registers xsd at http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema gets the prefix xsd_1, and the writer then declares a spurious xmlns:xsd_1 on prov:bundleContent.
A bundle with five namespaces writes its xmlns declarations in registration order. #337 (the declaration order depended on PYTHONHASHSEED), and HISTORY.md records the fix for PROV-XML.

Reading a record whose xsi:type attribute names prov:Plan, with and without extra inferred prov:type children, gives the PROV types the expected documents hold. The PROV-XML specification (https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-xml/) gives examples 4 and 5, and src/prov/tests/xml/README.txt says they are tested in test_xml.py because a round trip rewrites them.

Reading xml/example_06.xml gives a document equal to the one built in code for that example. The PROV-XML specification (https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-xml/) gives this example, and src/prov/tests/xml/README.txt records that the fixtures are its official examples.

Reading xml/example_07.xml gives a document equal to the one built in code for that example. The PROV-XML specification (https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-xml/) gives this example, and src/prov/tests/xml/README.txt records that the fixtures are its official examples.

A document whose default namespace is the PROV namespace reads an unprefixed value element as prov:value, and the document round trips through XML. #155, and HISTORY.md (the PROV-XML default namespace fix) records it.

An unprefixed xsi:type under an xmlns equal to the XML Schema IRI reads as the canonical xsd datatype, so a value of type int reads as the integer 1. The contract is #155, as the XML Schema half of the default-namespace fix, which commit dccdb208 added in the fix's review. The argument names `xml_qname_to_QualifiedName`, which passes a name with no prefix to `_bare_name`, and `_namespace`, which maps a prefixed xsd the same way, from reading, with no planted fault behind them.

Reading a document with an external entity still leaks no file text after the process-wide default lxml parser is replaced by one that resolves entities. #273 (PROV-XML parsing used lxml defaults), and docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-XML section).

An empty-string value survives an XML round trip as a plain attribute, as prov:label, as prov:value and as a language-tagged Literal. #224 (PROV-XML dropped attributes whose value is the empty string).

_escape_ncname_localpart then _unescape_ncname_localpart returns the input, and the escaped form is a valid lxml element tag, for plain, illegal, escape-shaped, boundary and astral names. docs/reference/conformance.md (C3) and #289 (the Private Use Area boundary fault).

Reading a document whose DOCTYPE declares an external SYSTEM entity does not raise, leaves the file's text out of the document and reads the value as empty. docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-XML section) says the reader does not expand a DOCTYPE entity and reads the text before the reference, and #273.

With force_types True the writer adds xsi:type to a plain string attribute, and with False it leaves that attribute untyped, while numbers, dates and prov:type stay typed. #338, and docs/howto/provxml.md (Write xsi:type on every attribute).

Removed, folded into test_xml.py::test_ncname_attribute_names_roundtrip_xml as the row "escape-lookalike" (#289). An attribute name that already looks like an _x0041_ escape survives an XML round trip as itself. The input arrives as f"ex:{local_part}" with local_part "_x0041_", the same string, the assertion is unchanged, and the #289 comment on the self-escape of the introducing underscore sits above the row. The verifier's fault in `_escape_ncname_localpart`, which appended "_" in place of "_x005F_", failed the row "escape-lookalike".

An attribute name whose local part holds one of ' ( ) , : ; [ ] = or starts with a digit, or that already looks like an _xHHHH_ escape, survives an XML round trip (#289, and C3 of docs/reference/conformance.md). Renamed from test_ncname_illegal_attribute_names_roundtrip_xml, because _x0041_ is a legal NCName, and it gained the row "escape-lookalike" from test_literal_ncname_escape_shaped_attribute_name_roundtrips_xml. The eight earlier ids stay. Both bodies built ex:e1 with one attribute and asserted the round trip, so the row gains no assertion. The verifier found the arcs of each row in src/prov unchanged by the merge, and the mutation run over provxml.py changed no mutant's status. The verifier's fault, `_escape_ncname_localpart` appending "_" in place of "_x005F_", failed the row "escape-lookalike" and the two escape-lookalike ids of test_xml.py::test_escape_unescape_ncname_localpart_is_inverse. The argument also names `_unescape_ncname_localpart`, the inverse the reader applies, from reading, with no planted fault behind it. No other test pinned a form that the row replaced.

Removed. Reading xml/nested_default_namespace.xml by path, where an entity element declares its own xmlns and a bare prov:id="e001" sits under a root that declares only prov, raised ProvXMLException that named the IRI http://example.org/0/ and the id, asserted as a regex and a substring. test_xml.py::test_a_name_with_no_prefix_under_an_elements_own_xmlns_is_refused takes over, because its rows read the same shape from a string and assert the full message that `_bare_name` raises (#677). The verifier's fault in `_bare_name` that dropped the IRI from the message failed all four rows of the takeover with this test deselected, and its fault that rejected only a root declaring just prov failed the rows "e-no xmlns" and ":e-no xmlns". The removal check found no arc that only the removed tests cover and no mutant of provxml.py or records.py that became undetected. The one separating fault found was a coordinator probe in the path branch of `ProvDocument.deserialize` that rewrote the file's bytes to drop every element-level xmlns="; only this test failed. The maintainer accepted the removal and named that fault as contrived. The fixture and its line in xml/README.txt went with the test.

A hadMember member wrapped in an extra entity element reads as the inner prov:ref, with a ProvWarning that says the reference is nested. docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-XML section) and HISTORY.md (the ProvToolbox hadMember shape).
The warning for a nested reference is a single ProvWarning attributed to the file that called deserialize. docs/development.md (a warning is attributed to the caller's frame).

A prov:document that holds a child element in a foreign namespace raises ProvXMLException whose message says a non-PROV element was found. The PROV-XML specification (https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-xml/) allows only PROV elements and prov:other in a document, and docs/reference/serializers.md lists ProvXMLException as the PROV-XML reader's error. With the namespace check in `ProvXMLSerializer.deserialize_subtree` deleted, the input raises from the unknown-name check in `ProvXMLSerializer._read_record` instead, and only this test fails in a whole-suite run.

Reading a document whose only content is a prov:other element raises one warning naming non-PROV information and leaves the document empty. docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-XML section) says prov:other elements are skipped with a warning. The test also checks that the warning is both a `ProvWarning` and a `UserWarning`, so a filter written for 3.3.0 still matches it (#826, and the `ProvWarning` docstring). It reaches the warning in `ProvXMLSerializer.deserialize_subtree`. Passing a plain `UserWarning` there fails this test alone in a whole-suite run. Making `_SkippedDataWarning` inherit from `ProvWarning` alone fails it with test_xml.py::test_unrepresentable_sub_element_attribute_warns_and_is_ignored, test_rdf.py::test_unmapped_subject_still_warns_and_is_named and test_malformed.py::test_rdf_foreign_vocabulary_parses_but_yields_empty_document, and inheriting from `UserWarning` alone fails it with test_xml.py::test_unrepresentable_sub_element_attribute_warns_and_is_ignored and test_rdf.py::test_unmapped_subject_still_warns_and_is_named.

A bare name under an xmlns equal to the PROV IRI resolves in the default namespace, and reading the primer example constructs each (prefix, IRI) Namespace once. planning/specs/2026-10-23-release-3.3.0-spec3-names-provn.md (3.4) describes one Namespace per (prefix, IRI) for the length of a read. Later audit: judge the direct-call section and the count section each on its own under rule 9.

An xmlns:ex redeclared on an element with the same IRI keeps one namespace, and one with a new IRI makes the QName value resolve in the new namespace. docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md (PROV-XML section) says a prefix declared in scope resolves.

A hadMember member given as element text reads as that reference, and no warning of any category is raised. docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md (PROV-XML section) says reference text resolves as a prov:ref does.

A document holding one typed entity serialises to XML that matches xml/example_06.xml after canonicalisation. The PROV-XML specification (https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-xml/) gives this example, and src/prov/tests/xml/README.txt records that the fixtures are its official examples.

A document holding one activity with times and a QName-typed prov:type serialises to XML that matches xml/example_07.xml after canonicalisation. The PROV-XML specification (https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-xml/) gives this example, and src/prov/tests/xml/README.txt records that the fixtures are its official examples.

A document holding two generations with times and a port attribute serialises to XML that matches xml/example_08.xml after canonicalisation. The PROV-XML specification (https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-xml/) gives this example, and src/prov/tests/xml/README.txt records that the fixtures are its official examples.

prov.sorted_attributes puts formal attributes first, then label, location, role, type and value, then the rest by name text and value text, and keeps input order for equal keys. prov.sorted_attributes is a frozen public name in src/prov/tests/test_public_api.py, and planning/specs/2026-10-27-release-3.3.0-spec4-performance.md (T1.1) says the order is unchanged.

Removed, folded into test_xml.py::test_unrecognised_only_attribute_on_a_sub_element_raises as the row "after-sibling" (#254, second mode). The XML input, the #254 comment and the three assertions carry over unchanged: UserWarning ignored, ProvXMLException raised, and "no representable value" in the message. The new name drops "not_reuses_value", and the comment keeps that story. The verifier's fault in `_extract_attributes`, the test `_v is _unassigned` made false, failed both rows of the merged test.

A child element whose only XML attribute is unrecognised raises ProvXMLException saying it has no representable value (#254). Merged from test_unrecognised_only_attribute_on_first_sub_element_raises (row "first-child", a first child that leaked an UnboundLocalError) and test_unrecognised_only_attribute_after_sibling_raises_not_reuses_value (row "after-sibling", a previous sibling's value reused silently). Both bodies were the same, so no row gains an assertion, and both XML strings carry over byte for byte with their #254 comments. Nothing is lost. The verifier found each row's arcs in src/prov unchanged by the merge, and the mutation run over provxml.py changed no mutant's status. The verifier's one fault, `_extract_attributes` with the test `_v is _unassigned` made false, failed both rows. No run shows that either row alone catches its own mode. No other test pinned a form that a row replaced.

Removed, folded into test_xml.py::test_unrecognised_only_attribute_on_a_sub_element_raises as the row "first-child" (#254, first mode). The XML input, the #254 comment and the three assertions carry over unchanged: UserWarning ignored, ProvXMLException raised, and "no representable value" in the message. The verifier's fault in `_extract_attributes`, the test `_v is _unassigned` made false, failed both rows of the merged test.

A child element that carries an unknown XML attribute warns that it is not representable and still reads its text as the value. docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-XML section) says attributes the model cannot represent are skipped with a warning. The test also checks that the warning is both a `ProvWarning` and a `UserWarning`, so a filter written for 3.3.0 still matches it (#826, and the `ProvWarning` docstring). It reaches the warning in `_extract_attributes`. Passing a plain `UserWarning` there fails this test alone in a whole-suite run. Making `_SkippedDataWarning` inherit from `ProvWarning` alone fails it with test_xml.py::test_other_elements, test_rdf.py::test_unmapped_subject_still_warns_and_is_named and test_malformed.py::test_rdf_foreign_vocabulary_parses_but_yields_empty_document, and inheriting from `UserWarning` alone fails it with test_xml.py::test_other_elements and test_rdf.py::test_unmapped_subject_still_warns_and_is_named.
An attribute name that is already a legal NCName is written unchanged, with no _x escape in the output. #289, and docs/reference/conformance.md (C3) says only illegal characters are escaped.

Reading xml/example_33.xml gives three membership records over one collection, and writing the document gives three hadMember elements. The PROV-XML specification (https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-xml/) example 33, and planning/specs/2026-10-28-release-3.3.0-spec5-defects.md (section 4.2).

A hadMember split into one record per entity equals the document the PROV-JSON reader builds from a list of members, and both write the same PROV-JSON text. HISTORY.md (the PROV-XML reader reads one hadMember record per entity, as the PROV-JSON and PROV-JSONLD readers do).

A hadMember element with several entities reads as one membership record per member, each with the element's identifier, collection, attribute and type, and a repeated member gives one record. docs/reference/conformance.md (PROV-XML section), HISTORY.md (#700) and #710.

The xmlns declarations of a document come out as ex, prov, xsd and xsi whether or not the document declares xsi itself. The contract is #510 and #337, because declaring xsi must not reorder the writer's output. The argument names `ProvXMLSerializer._build_nsmap`, which builds the declarations, from reading, with no planted fault behind it. PR #616 (commit 8f7f532f) added the test.

`xml_qname_to_QualifiedName`, called with no scope on a name with no colon under an element with no default, raises ProvXMLException saying no valid QualifiedName could be made. The contract is ruling N73 of planning/specs/2026-10-23-release-3.3.0-spec3-names-provn.md ("the reader's raise stays for a direct call with no scope"), and the spec's test list says this test stays. The function is undocumented and not in the frozen public API, and every reader call passes a scope.

A record with two activities, or a membership with two collections, raises ProvXMLException naming the element and saying more than one value. planning/specs/2026-10-28-release-3.3.0-spec5-defects.md (section 4.2) and HISTORY.md (a record holds one value of each PROV attribute).
Writing a document whose xsi prefix is bound to another IRI raises ProvXMLException naming both IRIs. docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md (The xsi prefix, #510) lists this exact message.

An xmlns on prov:bundleContent becomes that bundle's default namespace, and a bundle with none reads its bare names in the document's default. docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md (PROV-XML section) and planning/specs/2026-10-23-release-3.3.0-spec3-names-provn.md say an xmlns on prov:bundleContent is the bundle's default, the reader half of #572.

An xmlns on prov:document becomes the document's default namespace, and a bare prov:id reads as an identifier with an empty prefix and the IRI under that default. docs/howto/prepare-for-3-3.md (PROV-XML section) says an xmlns on prov:document is the document's default namespace in 3.3.0, and planning/specs/2026-10-23-release-3.3.0-spec3-names-provn.md says the reader registers it as the document's default.
